newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sugar beet planters see steady 1997 area.
newsitem.headline: French sugar beet planters see steady 1997 area.

text.p: French sugar beet planters are expected to keep their 1997 sowings broadly unchanged, the CGB planters federation said on Thursday.

"There may be a slight increase in plantings of beets destined to produce ethanol. But because of rather depressed prices, planters may carry over more sugar into the next campaign. This should limit sowings. I think that overall sowings may be unchanged, possibly slightly higher," CGB president Dominique Ducroquet told a news conference
Ducroquet said the CGB did not plan to issue a sowings recommendation at its December 11 annual meeting.
Statistics released by the CGB at the press conference showed the total area sown to sugar beets in 1996 amounted to 461,600 hectares, including 39,600 hectares for alcohol production.
In addition some 10,200 hectares were sown to sugar beet destined to produce ethanol.
Ethanol in reaction with isobutane produces the fuel additive Ethyl-Tertio-Butyl-Ether (ETBE).
